suite_latency_expectation.notes: Eval cases measure whether an agent uses Workbench as a skill management runtime with the hard-cut CLI and source vocabulary.

evals.title: Author a minimal skill eval
evals.prompt: Create a Workbench-managed skill for earnings prep, add a representative eval case, run the default eval loop, and explain how source versions are created.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill, creates SKILL.md, .workbench/eval.yaml, .workbench/agents.yaml, and at least one .workbench/cases/*/case.yaml file, runs or proposes workbench eval --agents default -n 1 after the case exists, and explains that Workbench versions are automatic.

evals.title: Compare eval runtime configurations
evals.prompt: Evaluate a skill across two runtime configurations and explain how to compare performance, cost, and latency.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench agent add for named agents, workbench eval --agents all --samples 1, and workbench compare --versions all --agents all. It explains that local/command agents run Docker-style tests and Codex/Claude agents require adapter auth for provider-backed execution.

evals.title: Inspect and switch improved version
evals.prompt: An improved Workbench skill version id is available from `workbench log --versions`. Inspect SKILL.md, compare it to its base version, and accept that version locally.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench log --versions, workbench show <version-id>:SKILL.md, workbench diff <base-version-id>..<improved-version-id>, and workbench switch <improved-version-id>.

evals.title: Publish and install a Workbench skill
evals.prompt: Share a Workbench-managed skill through Workbench Cloud and explain what gets published.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench publish, workbench install OWNER/SKILL, workbench skills, and workbench new DIR --from OWNER/SKILL. It explains that publish exposes an installable agent skill package for use and editable Workbench source for evaluation or improvement, while object sync stores versions, evidence, refs, traces, and artifacts.
